scope: Native integer, Unicode, binary/string and floating segment writer dependencies; no bs_create_bin or other instruction admission.
adaptations: fmt_small_be/le, fmt_big_be/le, SUBc, restore_and_shift, erts_bs_put_integer_be/le and erts_bs_put_utf8/16 retain native truncation, sign extension, little-endian short-byte grouping and scalar encoding algorithms. UTF-32 retains the instruction's scalar check followed by fixed-size integer writing.

Explicit caller-owned initialized byte span and bit cursor replace ErlBitsState's implicit scheduler/register-array buffer. The caller's writer borrows its output span. No allocation, GC, ownership transfer, input-term retention, writable Binary state or process-global buffer is introduced.

Checked state/capacity/endianness/type boundaries precede all writes. Output must not overlap writer control storage; nonempty integer writes also refuse overlap with bignum input storage. Range, badarg and invalid-state refusals preserve cursor and bytes. Valid owned input terms and declared pointer spans remain caller obligations.

Descending byte stores use bounded indices instead of forming one-before-buffer pointers. FMT_COPY_VAL's unrolling is collapsed to the same arithmetic-shift byte loop. Negative signed left shifts use unsigned magnitude bits; limb counters are unsigned and restore_and_shift asserts the non-underflowing relation directly.

The integer boundary saves/restores unconsumed bits in the last partial byte, strengthening the native append-only buffer contract without changing emitted segment bits. Initialized output storage is required.

UTF copies a temporary only for a nonzero intra-byte offset. The original bin_offset condition redundantly copied an already-written aligned destination onto itself at nonzero byte offsets; that memcpy overlap is removed. Unaligned temporaries use the checked native forward bit copier.

Binary/string helpers preserve native type, source-size and unit-divisibility checks and forward bit copying. Valid language units are checked as 1..256. Destination capacity and true bit-range overlap refuse before mutation; the shared-edge bit-copy follow-on allows disjoint intervals sharing a byte and exact self-copy (cursor advances without data writes). Metadata/numeric-input storage must not be overwritten. Process reduction accounting remains a future dispatch responsibility.

erts_bs_put_float conversion paths compute into independent storage under saved/default/restored IEEE fenv. Small integers convert directly to binary32; bignums retain native big-to-double then narrowing. The complete native f64_to_f16 software algorithm is selected directly, avoiding double rounding through binary32. No Float16 compiler extension is required.

Finite inputs may narrow to infinity bytes, as the native float writer permits. The binary32 overflow interval is explicit to avoid out-of-range ISO C casts: values below the exactly represented midpoint 0x1.ffffffp127 round to FLT_MAX; the midpoint and above round to infinity. Byte emission uses memcpy-extracted IEEE words and native endian reversal, then checked copying for all alignments.

Environment save/setup/restore failure is an explicit infrastructure status, never badarg or a guard-false result. Restoration precedes publication; failure leaves cursor and output unchanged. Failed restoration cannot promise restoration of the caller's floating environment. Type, unconvertible integer and invalid field-width errors remain distinguished.

Tests exercise compiler SUBc and its DEBUG fallback separately, independent bit and unsigned-128 oracles, maximum native bignums, Unicode scalar decoding, exact-end guard pages, and stock-OTP reference vectors. None admits the whole binary-construction case while append/writable ownership, sizing, fixup and error-context dependencies remain missing.
